title: Custom Layers – Build Your Own 🧱
description: Subclass tf.keras.layers.Layer to create reusable components with custom logic.

slides.title: Beyond Built‑in Layers 📦
slides.content:
# Why Custom Layers?

Sometimes you need a computation that isn't covered by existing layers:
- A new activation function.
- A layer with trainable parameters that combines inputs in a special way.
- A layer that applies a complex mathematical transformation.

Subclass `tf.keras.layers.Layer` and implement:
- `__init__` – define layer‑specific attributes.
- `build(input_shape)` – create weights (called on first call).
- `call(inputs, training=False)` – forward pass logic.

slides.title: A Simple Dense Layer (Custom)
slides.content: Create a Dense layer from scratch.

quizData.question: When is the `build` method of a custom layer called?

options.text: The first time the layer is called with an input shape

quizData.explanation: `build` is automatically invoked on the first call to `__call__`, which passes the input shape, allowing lazy weight creation.

slides.title: Adding Trainable & Non‑trainable Weights 🏋️
slides.content:
# `self.add_weight()`

- Create weights: `kernel = self.add_weight(name='kernel', shape=..., initializer=...)`.
- For non‑trainable weights (e.g., running mean in BatchNorm), set `trainable=False`.

You can also create standard variables with `tf.Variable`, but `add_weight` integrates with Keras saving/loading.

slides.title: Test Your Layer 🧪
slides.content: Always test with a sample input and check `.trainable_variables`. Use `layer.build(input_shape)` manually if you want to inspect weights before first call.
